# ButterKeys

> Local-first macOS menu bar app that corrects recurring personal typing mistakes (motor-pattern slips) in real time. Typing, but smoother.

ButterKeys is not a cloud spellchecker or grammar rewriter. It focuses on the finger slips you repeat — adjacent key swaps, early spaces, classics like teh→the — and stays quiet when unsure. Everything for correction runs on the Mac. No accounts. No analytics. No network required to correct text.

## Facts

- Product: ButterKeys
- Author: Tim Benniks
- Platform: macOS 14 or later (Apple Silicon preferred)
- Version: 1.0.0
- Price: Free

- Install guide: https://timbenniks.github.io/butterkeys/install.html

## What it does

- Real-time correction of recurring motor-pattern typos
- Teach personal rules from selection (Control-Option-T) or menu → Teach
- Learning suggestions can become real rules when accepted
- Undo last ButterKeys correction with Control-Option-Z
- Code editors default to a narrower “code-safe” mode
- Optional Sparkle update checks (no typing data in those requests)

## What it does not do

- Send keystrokes or sentences to the cloud
- Store full sentences or raw keystroke logs
- Monitor secure password fields
- Require an account
- Replace system spellcheck / Grammarly-style grammar rewriting

## Permissions required

- Input Monitoring (for the /Applications copy)
- Accessibility (for the /Applications copy)
- After granting both: quit and relaunch from Applications

## Privacy summary

Correction is local-only. Stored data is compact: explicit rules, learned typo pairs, motor-pattern aggregates, optional correction history, app policies, and settings. Never stored: full sentences, raw keystroke logs, passwords, clipboard contents.

## Quick test

In Notes, type `teh` and a space. It should become `the`. Undo with Control-Option-Z.
